import itertools
mod=3
points=[(x,y,z) for x in range(3) for y in range(3) for z in range(3)]
idx={p:i for i,p in enumerate(points)}
# get direction representatives (non-zero vectors modulo scalar)
vecs=[]
seen=set()
for v in points:
    if v==(0,0,0): continue
    # generate its two non-zero scalar multiples
    muls=[v, tuple((2*coord)%mod for coord in v)]
    rep=min(muls)  # lexicographic min as rep
    if rep in seen: continue
    seen.add(rep)
    vecs.append(v)
# we need 13 directions but only need 7 weeks; choose any 7
vecs7=vecs[:7]
weeks=[]
for v in vecs7:
    groups=[]
    used=set()
    for p in points:
        if p in used: continue
        # line through p in direction v
        line=[p]
        cur=p
        for _ in range(2):
            cur=tuple((cur[i]+v[i])%mod for i in range(3))
            line.append(cur)
        for pt in line:
            used.add(pt)
        groups.append([idx[pt] for pt in line])
    weeks.append(groups)
# verify each week has 9 groups of 3
assert all(len(g)==9 and all(len(gr)==3 for gr in g) for g in weeks)
# verify pair condition
pair_seen=set()
ok=True
for w,g in enumerate(weeks):
    for gr in g:
        for a,b in itertools.combinations(gr,2):
            if (a,b) in pair_seen:
                ok=False
            pair_seen.add((a,b))
            pair_seen.add((b,a))
print('ok',ok,len(pair_seen)//2)
# produce flat list week*27+player -> group index
flat=[]
for w,g in enumerate(weeks):
    group_of=[None]*27
    for gi,gr in enumerate(g):
        for p in gr:

    flat.extend(group_of)
